messages:
maria: heads-up — monitoring alerted a big jump in correctable ECC counts on node gpu-ap-east-3 (gpu-012). ~2k correctables since 02:15 UTC, small number of Xid 31s in dmesg. alert: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/gpu-ecc?panelId=4 :thinking_face:
jon: ack, saw it. Is this one of the older T4 racks?
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_ecc_correctable_total increase detected on gpu-ap-east-3 (rate 350/min over 10m). Incident ID INC-2026-0721-gpu-ecc. Auto-drain policy: OFF for this pool.
maria: correct — this pool still has autodrain disabled because of tight capacity in ap-east. thinking about enabling a temporary auto-drain rule for sustained spikes + Xid.
cheng: can we confirm if workloads are memory-heavy? my first pass: no OOMs in kube events, but two pods show heavy batch tokenization.
kevin: quick triage steps: 1) check nvml/dcgm metrics 2) tail dmesg for Xid patterns 3) if Xid fatal patterns or continuous > threshold -> cordon+drain node.
kevin: sample checks I run:
```
# DCGM exporter summary
curl -s http://gpu-ap-east-3:9400/metrics | grep ECC
# dmesg
ssh gpu-ap-east-3 'dmesg | egrep "NVRM: Xid|Ecc" | tail -n 50'
# per-gpu nvml ECC counters
python3 -c "from pynvml import *; nvmlInit(); h=nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0); print(nvmlDeviceGetDetailedEccErrors(h, NVML_SINGLE_BIT_ECC));"
```

maria: ran the dmesg — repeating lines: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f): 31, ChId:0001`, mostly on GPU0 and GPU2.

jon: what's our current alert rule? I think prom has: `gpu_ecc_correctable_total` rate > 200/min over 15m triggers a P2.

maria: right. but P2s just page #oncall. We want an automated remediation decision for clear hardware degradation. proposal: auto-drain when BOTH conditions met: 1) sustained correctable rate > 300/min for 10m AND 2) at least one Xid 31 or Xid 79 within same window. Also only if node has <50% critical pods (avoid draining critical capacity during peak).

tamara: +1 for two-factor rule (rate + Xid). we should also add a cooldown window so we don't thrash nodes with transient spikes. say disable auto-drain for 30m after a manual override.

cheng: operationally we need to update two places: Prometheus alert and the drain controller (k8s-drain-manager). here's a draft prom rule:
```
- alert: GPUCorrectableSpikeWithXid
  expr: |
    (
      increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[10m]) / 10 > 300
    ) and (
      count_over_time(gpu_nvml_xid_errors_total{code=~"31|79"}[10m]) > 0
    )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC correctable spike + Xid detected on {{ $labels.instance }}"
    runbook: "github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/gpu-ecc-autodrain"
```

kevin: looks good. for the drain-manager, I propose the flow: on alert trigger -> create remediation ticket and mark node cordoned (kubectl cordon) -> attempt graceful drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120` -> if drain stalls > 15m, escalate to infra oncall to decide whether to force evict -> once drained, label node `gpu_health=degraded` and reduce scheduling (taint + eviction) -> schedule replacement workflow.

maria: agree. a few edge cases: 1) multi-gpu nodes where only one GPU shows issues; draining whole node hurts capacity. can we instead isolate GPU via MIG or driver-level gating? 2) managed pools where draining triggers large reschedules.

jon: for MIG-capable hardware we can follow a different quickpath: disable the affected GPU device at the driver level (pci reset / nvidia-smi --gpu-reset) and only drain if errors return. add that to playbook.

tamara: we should add a manual opt-out label `gpu-autodrain=disabled` for critical nodes (retained for week).

cheng: logging + ticket template to create automatically (inc + hw tag + dcgm dump + three last dmesg snippets). we can wire that into the drain-manager. example ticket body:
```
Node: gpu-ap-east-3 (gpu-012)
Pool: ap-east-gpu-pool-3
Symptoms: sustained ECC correctable increase (rate ~350/min), Xid 31 seen in dmesg
DCGM: attached (dcgm-snapshot-1769123456.tgz)
Suggested action: cordon + drain for hardware replacement. Proc owner: eng-infra
```

maria: decision check: enable temporary auto-drain for ap-east pool with new rule, cooldown 30m, and enable MIG quickpath where possible. notify ap-east slack channel and oncall before flipping.

kevin: I'll make a PR to prom + drain-manager config. tagging @ops-bot to run a dry-run tonight at 23:50 UTC.

ops-bot: DRY-RUN scheduled: GPUCorrectableSpikeWithXid rule will be evaluated in dry-run mode (no remediation) on 2026-07-21 23:50 UTC.

jon: once PRs merged, let's add a short blurb to runbook about thresholds per card family (T4 vs A100) — older T4s have noisier ECC behavior so their thresholds can be higher.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll create the Slack notice and schedule the dry-run watch. if anything spikes again, paste dmesg + dcgm dump in this thread. :thumbsup:

kevin: 👍
